Challenge : space system idea game on scratch
summary:
*Project Summary: Hashir's Space Mission Design Game* This is an educational 2-level space mission game designed by Hashir for Junior Astronauts. Level 1 is Budget Management. The player has a budget of $1000 to design a rocket for Mars. They must strategically purchase four critical systems: SOLAR $100, WATER $300, OXYGEN $400, and FUEL $200. This teaches resource prioritization, showing that Oxygen is the most vital for survival in space. 

Level 2 is Mars Exploration. After launch, the rover lands on Mars. The instruction is "After you collect all the material touch your spaceship." The player drives the rover to collect rocks and materials for research, then returns to the spaceship to complete the mission. 

The game teaches STEM, budgeting, and NASA's real mission planning in a fun, interactive way for kids ages 6-12
details:
• Resource Allocation Phase: Players start with a fixed budget ($1000) and must strategically allocate funds to equip their rocket with critical survival and operational modules—specifically Solar panels ($100), Water systems ($300), Oxygen reserves ($400), and Fuel ($200) before launching.
  • Planetary Surface Exploration Phase: Once launched to Mars, the player controls a rover to navigate the landscape, collect essential scientific rock and material samples, and return them back to the spaceship to complete the mission objectives.
  • Mission Success: Successfully gathering all elements triggers a research clearance screen, highlighting the educational goal of sustainable space research and resource planning.
